embedding_queries.text: If p is a complex polynomial of degree N, then for every complex w the modulus of p at w is at most the supremum of the modulus of p on the closed unit disk times the N-th power of max of 1 and the modulus of w.

The bound is split into two cases according to the size of the modulus of w: when the modulus of w is at most 1 the right-hand side equals the norm and the claim is the definition of the supremum norm, and when the modulus of w is greater than 1 the factor is the N-th power of the modulus of w.
Define the auxiliary polynomial q of z as z to the N times p evaluated at 1 over z, the reciprocal or reflected polynomial, which satisfies q of 1 over w times w to the N equals p of w.
On the unit circle the modulus of the auxiliary polynomial q equals the modulus of p at the inverse point and is therefore at most the supremum norm of p on the closed unit disk.
By the maximum modulus principle a polynomial whose modulus is bounded on the unit circle has modulus bounded by the same constant on the whole closed unit disk.
